title: Mobile as a wide-open seaport town
summary: Mother's big Alabama family; Mobile was wide open, with a red light district Cootie saw delivering papers, and he knew nothing of drugs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: No. Did she have a big family, Cootie? Was it her sister who came?
It was a big family, yeah. A real big family.
No. They were all from Alabama.
A little town up there. What was it? I don't recall.
Tell me what you do -- tell me about Mobile in those days, what it was like. It was kind of wide open, wasn't it? Wasn't there plenty of life, plenty going on?
Because I guess, being a seaport.
Was it a little more open?
It was sort of a wide open town.
Were there a lot of, what, speakeasies and -- or was that not that far back, I guess, huh?
Prohibition was, what, in the early '30s?
That was before that. Well, I know they used to have a red light district. And I used to deliver papers. I was a paper boy.
But there was no traffic in dope or anything like that?
In those days there wasn't, really, was there? That much.
I guess maybe there was in New York. I don't know.
I didn't know nothing about things like that.
